paper.title: Latency-Aware Contextual Bandit: Application to Cryo-EM Data Collection

settings.name_in_paper: Latency-aware contextual bandit with linear regressor class F^l
unmapped: Each round has a random latency function l_j over subsets; the learner is charged time l_j(A_j) in [l_min, l_max] and the horizon T is continuous time (semi-Markov decision process)
Regret is measured against the optimal long-run average-reward policy: T*Gamma^* - E[q(T)]
Arm features, action sets and latencies drawn i.i.d. per round from an unknown distribution; number of arms n_j <= n_max
Learner needs n_max, l_min, l_max to set the projection interval [Gamma_min, Gamma_max]
Noise is conditionally 1-sub-Gaussian; mean reward psi_* in [-1,1]; reward of a subset is the sum of the arm rewards
settings.definition_quote: The learner observes: (i) the arm feature vectors X_j ... (ii) the action space A_j ⊆ 2^{[n_j]} containing subsets of arms; and (iii) a latency function l_j : A_j → R_{≥0}. The learner selects a subset of arms A_j ∈ A_j and observes semi-bandit feedback... The linear regressor class is defined as F^l = {x ↦ <θ, x> | θ ∈ R^d, ||θ|| ≤ 1}, where the context space is Ω^l = {x ∈ R^d | ||x|| ≤ 1}.

settings.name_in_paper: Latency-aware contextual bandit with general regressor class F
unmapped: Mean reward function psi_* belongs to a known general regressor class F (realizability), with values in [-1,1]; complexity measured by eluder dimension and sup-norm covering number
Each round has a random latency function l_j over subsets; time cost l_j(A_j) in [l_min, l_max]; horizon T is continuous time (SMDP)
Regret measured against the optimal long-run average-reward policy
Learner needs n_max, l_min, l_max and the class F (with access to a least-squares regression oracle)
settings.definition_quote: The learner is given a regressor class F that contains the bounded mean reward function psi_*, i.e., psi_* ∈ F. ... Each selected arm i yields a random reward y_{j,i} = psi_*(x_{j,i}) + eps_{j,i}, where psi_*: R^d → [-1, 1] is the bounded mean reward function unknown to the learner

symbols.n_max: maximum number of arms per round

conditions: oracle: COAF has exact mean reward estimates (hat mu_j = mu_j) every round

source.label: lm: coaf_orc
source.quote: Suppose the COAF algorithm runs with $\xi = 1$ and has exact mean reward estimates, i.e., $\hat{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_j = \boldsymbol{\mu}_j$ in every round $j$. Then, for any time horizon $T > 0$, the regret of COAF satisfies $R_T^C \leq \sqrt{U_T} + \frac{n_{\max} l_{\max}}{l_{\min}}$

results.notes: Oracle case (true means known), only learning Gamma^*; holds for any regressor class. Regret defined via means and compared to optimal average-reward policy, so pseudo-regret vs best policy. T is continuous time.

symbols.n_max: maximum number of arms per round
symbols.W_T: 8 d T beta(T n_max/l_min, delta) log((d lam l_min + T n_max)/(d lam l_min)), with sqrt(beta(n,delta)) = sqrt(lam) + sqrt(2 log(1/delta) + d log((d lam + n)/(d lam)))

results.notes: Regret R_T is defined as an expectation, yet the theorem states the bound holds with probability 1-delta; recorded as stated.

source.label: th: cmbub2
source.quote: Suppose $\psi_* \in \mathcal{F}$ and let $d_T = \dim_E (\mathcal{F}, \tfrac{l_{\min}}{T n_{\max}})$. For any $\delta > 0$, with probability at least $1 - 2\delta$, the regret of COAF with parameter $\xi \in (0, 1)$ at any time $T$ satisfies ...
